8:7.text: And if any one loves righteousness, her labors are virtues; for she teaches self-control and prudence, justice and courage; nothing in life is more profitable for men than these.
8:7.notes: Ch. 11 epigraph; was quoted partially with '[wisdom]'. CCC 1805 quotes it in a different translation.

9:13.text: For what man can learn the counsel of God? Or who can discern what the Lord wills?

9:14.text: For the reasoning of mortals is worthless, and our designs are likely to fail,
9:14.notes: Ends in a comma (sentence runs on into v.15). Ch. 11 does not quote it.

9:17.text: Who has learned thy counsel, unless thou hast given wisdom and sent thy holy Spirit from on high?

7:7.text: Therefore I prayed, and understanding was given me; I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.
7:7.notes: Checked for Ch. 11 (2026-10-06). Fetched 2026-10-15 in both RSVCE (bible-history.com) and RSV; they agree. Upgraded from single-source.

7:8.text: I preferred her to scepters and thrones, and I accounted wealth as nothing in comparison with her.
7:8.notes: Fetched 2026-10-15 in both RSVCE (bible-history.com) and RSV; they agree.

9:15.text: for a perishable body weighs down the soul, and this earthy tent burdens the thoughtful mind.
9:15.notes: Fetched 2026-10-15 in both RSVCE (bible-history.com) and RSV; they agree.

9:16.text: We can hardly guess at what is on earth, and what is at hand we find with labor; but who has traced out what is in the heavens?
9:16.notes: Fetched 2026-10-15 in both RSVCE (bible-history.com) and RSV; they agree.
